flawed_step: The claim that closure distributes over intersection is false. Only the inclusion cl(A∩B) ⊆ cl(A)∩cl(B) holds in general.
counterexample: X = ℝ with the usual topology, A = (0,1), B = (1,2). A∩B = ∅, so cl(A∩B) = ∅. But cl(A) = [0,1] and cl(B) = [1,2], so cl(A)∩cl(B) = {1} ≠ ∅.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. In ℝ, the intervals (0,1) and (1,2) do not overlap, so the closure of their intersection is empty. Their closures still share the point 1. In general only the inclusion cl(A∩B) ⊆ cl(A)∩cl(B) holds.
